- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows steady upward trend with no recent spike, but true outcome shows sharp drop or reversal, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% to account for mean reversion.
- After a model forecast spike (e.g., >+5% from prior), true outcome often corrects downward; apply “overshoot correction” by subtracting 2–5% from forecast peak.
- When sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.1), model often over-optimistically forecasts upward; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent high if sentiment is flat or declining.
- If true outcome deviates >5% from model in first 3–5 days of forecast horizon, assume lagged reaction; shift forecast downward by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, if model is consistently 5–10% below true outcome over 3+ consecutive days, apply “bias correction” by adding 2–5% to forecast starting from day 5.
